rules.statement: Status codes come only from StatusMapping, and the three adapters answer the same request identically.
guards: spring-boot:WebAdapterParityTest#the three adapters answer byte for byte alike
spring-boot:WebAdapterParityTest#the three adapters make the same decision event

rules.statement: Indeterminate is always 503; 500 is kept for unmodelled exceptions.
External cancellation never produces an Outcome, and the downstream is never called.
No failure or timeout of any SPI produces a Permit (P13).

A path with a dot segment after one decoding, in any encoding (including after removing path parameters, with an encoded ';' and with '\' as a separator), or longer than 2048 characters, or with a segment longer than 256 characters, is answered 400 before authentication.

A credential that is invalid (a token whose `roles` or `policies` claim is not an array of strings, or whose `attributes` claim is not an object, included), expired or revoked is evaluated as anonymous: a permit proceeds, and a deny answers 401 with the token-* problem type that names why (token-invalid, token-expired, token-revoked), never unauthorized.

Only verifying a request's token may count it as not revoked while the revocation store cannot be read (the reader throws RevocationUnavailableException: the documented exception to failing closed, which cosec.authentication.revocation.fail-closed turns off); a reader never answers "not revoked" for a read that failed, and any other error the revocation check reports fails the request with 503, never accepts the token.

A request that carries an API key is judged by the key alone, never by a token it also carries: an unknown, disabled or expired key is a rejected credential (evaluated as anonymous, a deny answers 401 token-invalid), and a key store that cannot be read answers 503.

Conditions read the request's host attributes: `http.header.<name>`, `http.origin`, `http.referer` and their hosts (in lower case) from the request's headers, and `request.attributes.<name>` from what the adapter knows besides HTTP (the gateway's route id). A DENY on them applies, and an ALLOW gated on them permits; they are never read as absent when the request carries them. A header sent more than once with the same value is that value; one sent with different values has none (PIP-12).
guards: spring-boot:WebAdapterParityTest#the three adapters give the engine the same host attributes
spring-boot:WebAdapterParityTest#the gateway gives the engine the route id

rules.statement: A gateway never forwards an identity a client sent: CoSec-Identity is stripped from every request before anything reads it, whatever the mode or cosec.enabled, and the routing filters send only the identity the pipeline verified on a permit for an authenticated principal (to a route that receives it, IDN-7), so no route or global filter can add one.
Only the verifier turns a token into a principal: no class of CoSec decodes a JWT, or reads its claims as a principal, without verifying its signature first.

A request that sends a header with different values, when any statement, policy condition, boundary or rate limit key of the documents its view reads reads that header (`http.header.<name>`, or `Origin` and `Referer` through `http.origin` and `http.referer`), is answered 400 before evaluation, whatever the effect of the statement and whether it applies to the request; identical repeats are one value, and a header no document reads is not checked.
guards: engine:CompiledDocumentTest#a document knows the headers it reads

rules.source: RFC 0006 §5.3.2; batch R6 (B-01 of the 7.x residue audit)
rules.statement: The authorization cookie is read as a token only when cosec.pipeline.allow-cookie-token is on, and it is off by default: a browser sends a cookie on its own, on a cross-site request too, so a host that turns it on defends against CSRF itself. With it off, a request whose only credential is that cookie is anonymous. A gateway keeps the cookie from a route whether or not it reads it (IDN-8).
guards: spring-boot:CoSecPipelineAutoConfigurationTest#the authorization cookie is a credential only with allow-cookie-token

rules.statement: A path with an empty segment before its end (`//`, also as removing a path parameter leaves it), an encoded separator (`%2F`, in either case) or a backslash (`\`, or `%5C` in either case) is answered 400 before authentication: a pattern reads them as segments of their own or as part of one, so a DENY would not match what a backend that merges slashes, decodes separators or reads a backslash as a separator serves. A trailing `/` is read as written, and a double-encoded separator (`%252F`, `%255C`) decodes to text.

A check by host code (`AuthorizationChecker`) never permits what enforcement would refuse to decide: an `http` path is normalized as a request's path is, one enforcement answers 400 for is a deny, and any other resource is held to a request path's length bounds.
guards: runtime:AuthorizationCheckerTest#a path enforcement refuses is never permitted
runtime:AuthorizationCheckerTest#a path is decided as enforcement normalizes it
runtime:AuthorizationCheckerTest#a resource longer than a request path can be is denied

rules.statement: The client address (`environment.ip`) is read once, from one party the host trusts, never from both the server's forwarded-header handling and CoSec's: without a forward-headers strategy, the connection's peer, or the `X-Forwarded-For` entry `max-trusted-index` places from the right; under `native` on Tomcat (configured, inferred from the cloud platform, or `server.tomcat.remoteip.*`), the address RemoteIpValve resolved; under `native` on Reactor Netty or Jetty, `X-Forwarded-For` alone, never the address the server forwarded. Startup fails under `framework` or a ForwardedHeaderFilter or ForwardedHeaderTransformer that rewrites, under `native` on a server CoSec cannot tell, with `max-trusted-index` set explicitly on Tomcat `native`, and with `max-trusted-index: 0` on Reactor Netty or Jetty `native`.
guards: spring-boot:ClientIpReadingsTest#without a strategy CoSec reads the peer and X-Forwarded-For
spring-boot:ClientIpReadingsTest#on Tomcat with the native strategy CoSec takes the valve's address
spring-boot:ClientIpReadingsTest#on Tomcat with the native strategy an explicit max-trusted-index fails startup
spring-boot:ClientIpReadingsTest#on Netty and Jetty with the native strategy CoSec reads the header only
spring-boot:ClientIpReadingsTest#a forwarded-header filter or transformer of the application fails startup unless it only removes
spring-boot:ClientIpReadingsTest#the native strategy on a server CoSec cannot tell fails startup
spring-boot:ClientIpReadingsTest#the starter fails startup with the reason
spring-boot:RealServerClientIpTest#a client cannot claim an internal address
spring-boot:RealServerClientIpTest#a denied client cannot claim another address

rules.statement: A client address the host reported that is not an address (`unknown`, an obfuscated identifier) is unavailable, never absent: a statement that reads `environment.ip` errs as on a missing external attribute (a DENY is Indeterminate unless `onMissing: nomatch`), and the blacklist cannot be read for it. A trusted `X-Forwarded-For` entry or a peer written with a port, brackets or a zone is read as its address, and several `X-Forwarded-For` lines are one list, in order.

A method holding an ASCII lower-case letter is 400 `invalid-request`, before authentication. HEAD is decided as GET: a route map's HEAD route wins, without one HEAD takes GET's route, and unmapped it is `http:GET`; `http:HEAD` matches nothing unless a route map maps it.
